lines.japanese:
昼休みになったとたん、今まで授業に一時間も出てなかった男がやってきた。
「よう遠野！
　メシ食おうぜ、メシ！」
　何が嬉しいのか、有彦はとにかく威勢がいい。
lines.label: s244
lines.maoEnglish:
The instant lunch break began, a certain boy who hadn’t attended a single class all morning finally showed up.
“Yo, Tohno! Let’s eat! Lunch, lunch!” Whatever had him so delighted, Arihiko was bursting with energy.

lines.maoEnglish:
“Boy, she really hates you, Tohno! I’m so happy to have one less rival that lunch is on me today!” Arihiko gleefully pounded me on the back. “…I’m glad you’re paying, but was she angry with me?”
“Hm? Let me think. She asked, ‘Will Tohno be there too?’ When I nodded, her face turned red. Perchance her cheeks flushed with rage the instant she heard your name.” “Perchance? Since when do you talk like that, Arihiko?” “Who knows? Perchance not.”

lines.maoEnglish: Arihiko and I sit together for lunch. Our cafeteria has a television, and for reasons poised delicately between educational and appalling, it plays a recording of that morning’s news. The current story concerns a drunken customer stabbing a convenience-store clerk to death—exactly the sort of report that makes you avoid convenience stores for the next three days.

lines.maoEnglish: Going straight home seemed dull, so I decided to wander around town.
lines.mao_english: Going straight home seemed dull, so I decided to wander around town.
lines.mirrorMoon: I don't feel like returning to the mansion directly, so I'll wander around the city for a bit.
lines.mirror_moon: I don't feel like returning to the mansion directly, so I'll wander around the city for a bit.

lines.japanese:
―――かといって、アテもなく駅前にやってきても何があるというワケでもない。
　遠野の屋敷に引っ越してからの遠野志貴の財政事情はとても厳しいので、ここで散布をするのも気が引ける。
lines.label: s252
lines.maoEnglish:
Of course, arriving at the station with no destination did not magically provide anything to do.
Since moving into the Tohno estate, Shiki Tohno’s finances had become painfully tight. Squandering money here was out of the question.
lines.mao_english:
Of course, arriving at the station with no destination did not magically provide anything to do.
Since moving into the Tohno estate, Shiki Tohno’s finances had become painfully tight. Squandering money here was out of the question.
lines.mirrorMoon:
---I arrive in front of the station for no apparent reason.
Ever since I was invited back to live in the Tohno mansion, I've been low on money, so I really don't want to spend any money here.
lines.mirror_moon:
---I arrive in front of the station for no apparent reason.
Ever since I was invited back to live in the Tohno mansion, I've been low on money, so I really don't want to spend any money here.

lines.japanese:
有間の家にいたころは啓子さんから幾ばくかのお小遣い……華道で使用する和室の掃除や庭の手入れの報酬……を貰っていたけど、屋敷に帰ってからはそんな収入は望めないだろう。
　アルバイトぐらいしたいんだけど、それはきっと秋葉のヤツが許してはくれまい。
lines.label: s252
lines.maoEnglish: When I lived with the Arima family, Keiko gave me a little pocket money in return for cleaning the Japanese-style room used for flower arranging and tending the garden. There would be no such income now that I had returned to the estate. I would gladly take a part-time job, but Akiha would never allow it.
lines.mao_english: When I lived with the Arima family, Keiko gave me a little pocket money in return for cleaning the Japanese-style room used for flower arranging and tending the garden. There would be no such income now that I had returned to the estate. I would gladly take a part-time job, but Akiha would never allow it.
lines.mirrorMoon:
When I lived at the Arimas', Keiko-san would always give me some money for cleaning or tending the garden…… but now that I'm at the mansion, I don't think I can hope for that kind of income.
I'd like to do a part time job, but Akiha would never allow it.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
「……………はあ」
　今更ながら自分の複雑な立場を思い知って、ため息をつく。
lines.label: s252
lines.maoEnglish: I let out a long sigh. The complications of my position were sinking in all over again.
lines.mao_english: I let out a long sigh. The complications of my position were sinking in all over again.
lines.mirrorMoon:
……………… *sigh*
Reflecting on my complicated situation, I let out a sigh.
lines.mirror_moon:
……………… *sigh*
Reflecting on my complicated situation, I let out a sigh.

lines.japanese:
何をするわけでもなく、通りすぎていく人々を眺めていた。
　それも一時間ほどたって、はた、と自分が無意味な事をしている事に気がつく。
lines.label: s252
lines.maoEnglish: I did nothing but watch people pass. An hour slipped by before it struck me how utterly pointless this was.
lines.mao_english: I did nothing but watch people pass. An hour slipped by before it struck me how utterly pointless this was.
lines.mirrorMoon:
Not doing anything, I watch the people passing by.
I pass the time like that for an hour until I realize how pointless it is.
lines.mirror_moon:
Not doing anything, I watch the people passing by.
I pass the time like that for an hour until I realize how pointless it is.

lines.japanese:
「……何してるんだろ、俺」
　自分でもよくわからない。
　ただこうして人の流れを眺めていれば、その中に金の髪をなびかせて歩く誰かの姿を見つけ出せるかもしれない、とでも思ったのだろうか。
lines.label: s252
lines.maoEnglish: “What am I doing?” I didn’t know myself. Had I imagined that if I watched the crowd long enough, I might glimpse someone with golden hair streaming behind her?
lines.mao_english: “What am I doing?” I didn’t know myself. Had I imagined that if I watched the crowd long enough, I might glimpse someone with golden hair streaming behind her?
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… What the heck am I doing?"
I don't know for sure myself.
Was I thinking that I would see someone with golden hair walking by if I watched all these people?
lines.mirror_moon:
"…… What the heck am I doing?"
I don't know for sure myself.
Was I thinking that I would see someone with golden hair walking by if I watched all these people?

lines.japanese:
「……バカらしい。
アルクェイドとはもう会わないんだろ、志貴」
　寄りかかっていた壁から離れて、未練を断つように屋敷への帰途についた。
lines.label: s252
lines.maoEnglish: “This is stupid. You’re never seeing Arcueid again, remember?” I pushed away from the wall and turned toward the estate as though tearing myself free of the lingering hope.
lines.mao_english: “This is stupid. You’re never seeing Arcueid again, remember?” I pushed away from the wall and turned toward the estate as though tearing myself free of the lingering hope.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… How stupid.
You'll never see Arcueid again, Shiki."
I stop leaning on the wall and head back to the mansion.

lines.japanese:
坂をのぼりきって、屋敷に帰ってきた。
　時刻はまだ夕方の六時前。
　夕食まであと一時間、部屋で時間を潰すとしようか―――
lines.label: s252
lines.maoEnglish: I climbed the hill and returned to the estate. It was not yet six. With an hour until dinner, I might as well kill time in my room—
lines.mao_english: I climbed the hill and returned to the estate. It was not yet six. With an hour until dinner, I might as well kill time in my room—
lines.mirrorMoon:
I walk up the road and back to the mansion.
It's not quite six o'clock yet.
There's still an hour until dinner, so I'll kill some time in my room---
lines.mirror_moon:
I walk up the road and back to the mansion.

lines.japanese:
―――夕食が終わって、夜。
　居間には珍しく秋葉、琥珀さん、翡翠というフルメンバーが残っていて、俺も食後の紅茶をいただくことにした。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
Night, after dinner.
For once, the full complement—Akiha, Kohaku, and Hisui—has remained in the sitting room, so I join them for tea.
lines.mao_english:
Night, after dinner.
For once, the full complement—Akiha, Kohaku, and Hisui—has remained in the sitting room, so I join them for tea.
lines.mirrorMoon:
---Dinner is over, and it is now nighttime.
A rare event, Akiha, Kohaku-san, and Hisui are all in the sitting room, so I join them for some after-meal tea.
lines.mirror_moon:
---Dinner is over, and it is now nighttime.
A rare event, Akiha, Kohaku-san, and Hisui are all in the sitting room, so I join them for some after-meal tea.

lines.japanese:
「そうでしょうか。
わたし、一番目より二番目のほうが好きですね。
あっちのほうが味に品があるとは思いますけど」
「難しいわね。
味は格段に違うんだけど、濃度の違いをどうとるかは人それぞれだから。
けど、どのみち琥珀は日本茶のほうが好きなんでしょう？
　紅茶党は翡翠のほうだったと思うけど」
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“Really? I prefer the second one to the first. The other may have a more refined flavor, but still.”
“It’s difficult to say. The flavors are worlds apart, but whether you prefer one strength to the other is a matter of taste. In any case, Kohaku, don’t you favor green tea? I thought Hisui was the black-tea enthusiast.”
lines.mao_english:
“Really? I prefer the second one to the first. The other may have a more refined flavor, but still.”
“It’s difficult to say. The flavors are worlds apart, but whether you prefer one strength to the other is a matter of taste. In any case, Kohaku, don’t you favor green tea? I thought Hisui was the black-tea enthusiast.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Is that so?
I like the second one rather than the first one.
I think the taste is more refined."
"It's a difficult choice.
The difference in taste is great, but everyone handles the different concentrations in varied ways.
But, Kohaku, you like Japanese tea better, right?
I think Hisui prefers English tea."

lines.japanese:
「翡翠ちゃんはあんまりブランドにこだわりませんよ。
神経質そうに見えますけど、翡翠ちゃんはわりと―――」
「姉さん」
「―――見た目どおりに神経質なんですから。
ほら、お掃除とかお裁縫とか、できない事ってないんですよ、志貴さん」
　と、唐突に琥珀さんは俺に話をふってくる。
　翡翠の眼差しは、なんだか恐いし。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hisui doesn’t care much about brands. She may look fussy, but she’s actually rather—”
“Kohaku.”
“—rather as fussy as she looks. Why, whether it’s cleaning or sewing, there’s nothing she can’t do, Shiki.”
Without warning, Kohaku tosses the conversation to me.
And Hisui’s stare is frankly terrifying.

"Nee-san."
"---sensitive like she looks.

Kohaku-san suddenly engages me in conversation.
Hisui's glance seems… somewhat scary too.

「……そこでなんで俺にふるかな、琥珀さんは」
「だって志貴さんは翡翠ちゃんと一緒ですから。
翡翠ちゃんの神経質なところは知っているでしょう？」
「いや、それは―――」
　ちらり、と翡翠のほうを見る。
「……………………」
　……翡翠は無言で、なにか攻撃色を発しているし。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Why would you drag me into this, Kohaku?”
“Because Hisui looks after you, Shiki. Surely you know how particular she can be?”
“No, I wouldn’t say—”
I glance at Hisui.
“…”
…She is silently radiating something very much like an intent to attack.

"……………………"

「―――いや、別に神経質っていうコトはないんじゃないかな。
俺がポカやってもすぐに片付けてくれるし、夜遅くに帰っても誰かさんみたいに怒らないし」
「兄さん。
門限を守れない人は怒られて当然なんだって、わかってる？」
「……承知してる。
けどさ、いくらなんでも八時っていうのは早すぎないか？
　子供じゃないんだから、このさい十時ぐらいに決めなおそう」
「却下です。
兄さんにはそんな時間まで外にいる理由なんてないでしょう。
塾にかよっている訳でも部活をしている訳でもないんですから」
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“No, I wouldn’t call her fussy. Whenever I make a mess, she cleans it up right away, and when I come home late, she doesn’t get angry like a certain someone.”
“Brother. You do understand that anyone who breaks curfew deserves to be scolded?”
“…I do. But eight o’clock is absurdly early, isn’t it? I’m not a child. Let’s revise it to ten.”
“Denied. You have no reason to remain out that late. You neither attend cram school nor belong to a club.”

"---No, I don't think she's that sensitive.
She takes care of things quickly even when I mess something up, and she doesn't get angry like someone else when I come home late."
"Nii-san, don't you know it is perfectly natural for someone who breaks curfew to be scolded?"

I'm not a little kid, so let's make it like ten o'clock from now on."
"I refuse.
You don't have any reason to stay out that late anyway.
It's not like you have a cram school or a club to attend."

lines.japanese:
「……………む」
　そう言われると、こっちとしては立場が弱い。
　俺のような自由人が家に帰ってこない、という理由はその大部分が遊びになってしまうからだ。
「志貴さん、秋葉さまの言うとおりですよ。
近頃は物騒なんですから、あんまり夜の街を出歩かないでくださいね」
「―――物騒って、例の通り魔のこと？」
　はい、と琥珀さんは頷く。
　……なんか、つい笑ってしまう。
　通り魔殺人をしでかしていたネロはもういない。
　けどそれを知っているのは俺とアルクェイドだけで、世間の人たちはもはや不在になった通り魔という影に怯えているなんて。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Ngh.”
Put that way, I don’t have much ground to stand on. For a free spirit like me, staying out late usually amounts to nothing more defensible than having fun.
“Miss Akiha is right, Shiki. The city has been dangerous lately, so please don’t wander around at night.”
“Dangerous? You mean that serial killer?”
Kohaku nods.
…I almost laugh. Nrvnqsr, the creature behind those random killings, is gone. Yet only Arcueid and I know that; everyone else is still afraid of the shadow of a killer who no longer exists.

「今朝も繁華街のほうで被害者が発見されたそうですから。
これで十一人目ですよ、十一人目」
「……へえ、十一人目か。
そりゃあすごいな、野球ができ―――」
―――――ちょっと、待った。
「琥珀さん！」
「はい？」
「今の話、本当なのか！？」
lines.label: s253

“They found another victim downtown this morning. That makes eleven now. Eleven.”
“…Eleven, huh? Impressive. Enough for a baseball—”
Wait.
“Kohaku!”
“Yes?”
“Is that true?”

“What—”

Nrvnqsr is dead. He died two days ago. How could he claim another victim the following night?

Then why—
“…”
It seems impossible.
But if the vampire terrorizing the city is gone and the killings have continued, then only one other vampire remains here.

「アルクェイド……のハズはない、よな」
　あいつは人の血は吸わないって言ってたし、なにより―――あんなに人間くさいヤツが、そんなコトをするなんて思えない。
　あいつとはたった二日しか一緒にいなかったけど、悪いヤツじゃないって信じてる。
　あんなにキレイで、あんないい顔で笑うヤツが人の血を吸って、死体を道に捨てていくなんて酷いことをするハズがない。

“…”
There is another victim. Another body left by a vampire.
“It can’t have been…Arcueid. Can it?”
She said she never drinks human blood. More than that, I can’t imagine anyone so painfully human doing such a thing. I only spent two days with her, but I believe she isn’t evil. Someone so beautiful, someone who smiles with such open delight, could never drink a person’s blood and throw the corpse away in the street.

lines.label: s253

　ネロとの一戦以来しまっておいたナイフを取り出して、足音を立てないように屋敷から外に抜け出す。
　夜の街に出て、アルクェイドの姿を探しはじめた。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
Once I say it aloud, the rest comes quickly. I retrieve the knife I put away after the fight with Nrvnqsr and slip out of the estate without a sound.
Then I take to the night streets and begin searching for Arcueid.

lines.mirrorMoon:

I take the knife I used to fight Nrvnqsr and sneak quietly out of the mansion.
Going out into the street, I start to search for Arcueid.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
「―――はあ、はあ、はあ」
　足を止めて、呼吸を整える。
　今まで走りづめだった体が、ぜいぜいと貪欲に酸素を取り入れようとする。
「はあ―――はあ―――はあ」
　……だめだ、見つからない。
　街中を走りまわって、アルクェイドの部屋にも行ってみたけれど、あいつの姿はてんで見つからない。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hah…hah…hah…”
I stop and try to catch my breath. After running without pause, my lungs claw greedily for air.
“Hah…hah…hah…”
No good. I can’t find her. I’ve run all over the city and even checked her room, but there is no sign of Arcueid anywhere.

「……あいつ……どうでもいい時はひょこひょこ歩いてるクセに、どうして肝心な時はどこにもいないんだ……！」
　つい、身勝手にぐちを言ってしまう。
　あれから四時間。
時刻はじき午前零時になろうっていうのに、アルクェイドは見つからない。
　……なんとなく。
　なんとなく、捜せばすぐに見つかるだろう、なんて楽観をしていた。
　俺はあいつに会いたかったし、あいつだって別れ際に『またね』なんて言ってたし。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Why is she always strolling around whenever it doesn’t matter, but nowhere to be found when I actually need her…?”
The selfish complaint slips out. Four hours have passed. It is nearly midnight, and I still haven’t found Arcueid.
…Somehow, I had simply assumed I would find her as soon as I looked. I wanted to see her, and when we parted she had said, “See you.”

"…… That Arcueid…… She's always around when you don't need her, but when you try to find her……!"
I speak those words selfishly.
It's been four hours.
It's almost midnight, but I still don't see Arcueid anywhere.
…… For some reason.
For some reason, I thought optimistically that I'd find her easily once I started looking for her.
I want to see her, and when we last parted, she said "See you later."

「くそ……何処いったんだよ、アルクェイド……！」
　なにか、すごく苛々する。
　せっかくまた会えるって思ったのに会えないなんて、これじゃ生殺しみたいなものじゃないか。
「……せっかく……また、会えるって………」
―――？
　なんだろう、それは。
　それじゃまるで、その……俺が、アルクェイドに片思いでもしてるみたいじゃないか。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“Damn it… Where are you, Arcueid…?”
I’m furious, absurdly so. I thought I would finally see her again, and being denied at the last moment is unbearable.
“…I thought…I’d finally see you again…”
What?
What was that supposed to mean? It makes it sound as if I’m…as if I’m in love with Arcueid.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Shit…… Where did you go, Arcueid……!"
For some reason, I'm getting very annoyed.
I keep thinking I'll see her soon but I don't.
This is killing me.

"…… I…… thought…… we'd see each other again………"
---?
What is that?
It's like…… I'm in love with her.

「―――そんな」
「―――ばかな」
　無理やりに苦笑して、つまらない考えを振り払う。
「……最後に公園を見て、それで見つからなかったら帰るか」
　ふう、と大きく息をはいて公園へ歩き出す。
　二日前の夜。
　アルクェイドと別れた、いわくつきの公園へ。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“That’s…”
“That’s idiotic.”
I force a crooked smile and shake off the ridiculous thought.
“…I’ll check the park one last time. If she isn’t there, I’m going home.”
With a long breath, I start walking.
Toward the park where Arcueid and I parted two nights ago, a place already heavy with bad memories.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"---But that---"
"---That's stupid."
Forcing a grim smile, I shake that thought from my mind.
"…… I'll check out the park, and if I don't see her there, I'll go back."
Taking a deep breath, I walk to the park.
Two nights ago.
That park where so much happened, the park where I parted with Arcueid.

「―――ん？」
　何か、公園の様子がいつもと違う。
「………街灯がついてない」
　公園中の街灯が消えてしまっている。
　月明かりでうっすらと見える公園は、いつにもまして活気というものがなかった。
「なんだろ……停電かな」
　きょろきょろとあたりを見渡す。
　……公園の外の街灯はきちんとついている。
　街灯がついていないのは、公園の中だけらしい。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hm?”
Something about the park is different.
“…The lights are out.”
Every lamp inside the park is dark. Beneath the thin moonlight, the grounds look even more lifeless than usual.
“What happened…a blackout?”
I scan the area. The streetlamps outside are working normally. Only the lights within the park have failed.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"---Hm?"
There's something different about the park.
"……… The lamp posts are off."
The lamp posts throughout the park are all turned off.
The moonlit park seems more solitary than usual.
"Hmm…… is it a power outage?"
I look around me.
…… Outside the park, the lights are all working.
The only lamps not working are within the park itself.

――――キィィィン―――――
「え――――なんだ、いまの」
　なにか、耳をすますと音が聞こえてくる。
　ケンカとか争いごととか、そんなような事をしているような雑多な音の群れ。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
A long metallic shriek—
“What—what was that?”
When I listen closely, I can hear something: a confused tangle of noises, like a brawl or some other violent struggle.

lines.mirrorMoon:
-----Clang-----
"Eh----What was that just now?"
I can hear something.
The clamor sounds like it's coming from a fight.
lines.mirror_moon:

"Eh----What was that just now?"

lines.japanese:
「―――――」
　気にかかる。
　根拠なんてまったくないけれど、こんな夜更けに、なにやらトラブルくさいことを起こしているのはアイツぐらいだと思うのだ。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“…”
I can’t ignore it. I have no evidence at all, but at this hour, there is only one person I can imagine stirring up that kind of trouble.
lines.mao_english:

"-----"
I'm curious.
There's no basis for this, but this late at night, if there's any sort of trouble going on, I think it has to involve her.

lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“…All right.”
Moving as quietly as I can, I creep toward the noise.

"……… Alright."
Trying as hard as I can to be silent, I head towards the source of the sound.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
「――――！」
　向こうで二つの人影が争っている。
　一人は真っ黒い服装をしていてよくわからない。
　けどもう一人ははっきりとわかる。
　白い服装に、月明かりだけでもはっきりと見てとれる金の髪。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“—!”
Two figures are fighting in the distance. One is dressed entirely in black, too indistinct to make out. The other is unmistakable: white clothes and golden hair bright even beneath the moon.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"----!"
I can see two figures facing off.
Someone is wearing dark black garments and I can't tell who it is.
But I can easily tell the other one.
White garments, and golden hair that can be easily spotted even in just the moonlight.
lines.mirror_moon:
"----!"

lines.japanese:
「……アルクェイド……！」
　アルクェイドは、何か黒い人影に襲われていた。
　黒い人影は剣のようなものを持っていて、とてもケンカとかいったレベルの争いじゃない。
　人影は剣を構えてアルクェイドへと跳びかかる。
　アルクェイドは自分の胸に突き刺さろうとする剣を手で弾くと、そのまま剣を持った人影の胸にトン、と軽く触れた。
　次の瞬間。
　剣を持った人影は、サッカーボールか何かのように大きく弾き飛ばされていた。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Arcueid…!”
A black figure is attacking her.
The figure in black carries something like a sword. Whatever this is, it is far beyond a mere fight.
The figure raises the blade and springs at Arcueid. She bats aside the thrust aimed at her chest, then gives her attacker’s breast the lightest tap.
The next instant, the blade-wielding figure goes flying like a soccer ball.

"…… Arcueid……!"
Arcueid is being attacked by this black human shape.

Arcueid deflects the blade coming in towards her chest with her hand and lightly contacts the chest of that black shape.

that sword-wielding shape flies through the air like a soccer ball.

　公園のレンガ道の上に落下して、そのまま受身をとるように転がっていく。
　いや、正しくは。
　そのまま、俺の目の前に転がってきた。
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
Bam. Ba-bump-bump-bump.
The figure crashes onto the park’s brick path and rolls with the impact. No—to be precise, it comes rolling straight to my feet.

lines.mirrorMoon:

Falling down on the brick pathway in the park, it keeps rolling as if easing the fall.
No, to be more accurate,
it rolls right toward me.

　暗くてよく解らないけど、人影はちょうど俺の目の前で転がるのをやめて、素早く態勢をたてなおす。
「くっ――――！」
　という、切迫した声。
「は……あ」
　その動きに見惚れて、思わず感嘆の息をつく俺。
lines.label: s253

“…?”
It is too dark to see clearly, but the figure’s tumble ends directly before me. In an instant, the attacker regains balance.
“Ghh—!”
The voice is sharp with urgency.
“Ha…”
I can only stare, breath escaping me in wonder at the grace of that recovery.

"Ku-----!"
A sharp, cut-off voice.
"Haa…… ah."
Fascinated by this display, I let out a breath of admiration.

lines.label: s253

Then—perfect stillness.
The blade-wielding figure freezes.
“You saw me—!?”
Only now does the figure seem to notice me standing there. The blade snaps back into guard, and its wielder lunges into my space.

the sword-carrying figure ceases all movement.

The figure finally seems to realize I'm here.

「――――え？」
　刀の切っ先が、こちらの喉に伸びてくる。

踏み込んでくるスピード、的確な急所への一撃は、ネロのケモノどころの話じゃない。
　人影の動きは、ネロのケモノたちを蹴散らしていた時のアルクェイドに動きに匹敵していた。

lines.maoEnglish:
“What—?”
The point streaks toward my throat. The speed of that step, the precision of the strike at a vital point—Nrvnqsr’s beasts were nothing beside it. The figure moves as fast as Arcueid did when she tore those creatures apart.
With a tiny snick, the sword’s point pricks my throat.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"----Eh?"
The cutting blade of the sword rapidly arcs towards my throat.

This flying speed, this accuracy, surpasses that of Nrvnqsr's beasts.

　けどまあ、自己保身のために自らの痕跡を隠蔽する、というのは正しいわ」
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Because humans aren’t stupid. If they knew monsters like that lived among them, they would fight back. Humans may be weak, but we have the police and plenty of other ways to defend ourselves. If vampires were exposed, people would take precautions to prevent more deaths. They’d stop going out at night, like they have in this city. That would make hunting difficult, so vampires hide what they are.”
“That is part of it, I suppose. But the police are an institution of human law, meant to deal with humans. Creatures like us don’t even take them into account.
Still, you’re right that vampires erase their traces to protect themselves.”

lines.japanese:
「志貴、吸血鬼には天敵がいるのよ。
それも今ではパワーバランスはそっちのほうが上っていう、殺し屋みたいな集団がね。
　……他の超越種たちもそうだけど、とくに吸血種は自らの存在を明かしては命とりになる。
　たとえ小さな、文明社会から隔離された山村一つを支配して秘密の王国を作っても、犠牲者が増えればかならず彼らが嗅ぎ付けるから。
　吸血鬼たちが秘密裏に人間を搾取するのは何のためでもない、ただ自己保身のためだけよ。
彼らは社会的な風聞ではなく、その天敵に嗅ぎ付けられる事を嫌って自然に死体を隠蔽するの」
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“Vampires have a natural enemy, Shiki—a whole band of killers, and these days the balance of power favors them.
…Other transcendent species face the same danger, but for a vampiric species in particular, revealing its existence can be fatal. A vampire might rule one tiny mountain village cut off from civilization and build a secret kingdom there, but once enough victims accumulate, those enemies will inevitably catch the scent.
Vampires prey on humanity in secret for one reason alone: self-preservation. They don’t hide bodies to avoid rumors. They hide them so their natural enemy won’t find them.”

lines.japanese:
「……それも人間じゃない生き物なのか？」
「何いってるのよ。
その天敵っていうのは紛れもなくあなたたち人間の事よ」
「────？
　天敵って、俺たちが？」
「そう。
もうずっと昔、人間は様々な魔術、神秘学、式典儀礼をもとに組織体系を作り、人間以外の霊長類を排除しはじめたの。
　その最たる物が基督教───法王庁が誇るエクシシストの集団よ。
旧教（カトリック）は昔っから『人間でないモノ』を徹底的に淘汰してきたけど、その中でも吸血鬼に対する敵視はどうかしてるわ」
lines.label: s253
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Are they another kind of nonhuman creature?”
“What are you talking about? Their natural enemy is unquestionably humanity.”
“—? Humans are?”
“Yes. Long ago, humans built organizations upon various forms of magecraft, mysticism, and religious ritual, then began exterminating nonhuman primates.
The foremost example is Christianity—the corps of exorcists maintained by the Holy See. Catholicism has always purged anything ‘not human’ with ruthless thoroughness, but its hatred of vampires is deranged even by those standards.”
lines.mao_english:

“What are you talking about? Their natural enemy is unquestionably humanity.”
“—? Humans are?”
“Yes. Long ago, humans built organizations upon various forms of magecraft, mysticism, and religious ritual, then began exterminating nonhuman primates.
The foremost example is Christianity—the corps of exorcists maintained by the Holy See. Catholicism has always purged anything ‘not human’ with ruthless thoroughness, but its hatred of vampires is deranged even by those standards.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… So, they aren't human either?"
"What are you saying?
Their natural enemy is without a doubt you humans."
"-----?
Natural enemies, us?"
"Yeah.
Starting from a long time ago, humans used many kinds of magic, the occult, magical ceremonies to create an organization and started to eliminate primates other than humans.
The greatest of these is Christianity---the pride of the Vatican, the Exorcists.
The Catholic Church always viewed "nonhumans" as impurities, but vampires are considered the most dangerous."

The English keeps only happiness and anger. “No. That thing was certainly marked for execution, but returning one of the Dead like that to dust is not my objective. I disposed of it because it was my enemy’s thrall. Even a creature like that will kill people and accumulate power if left alone.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Well, as you wish, Shiki, let's talk about anything.
If you want to ask something, feel free."
"Then I'll ask, but just what was that guy earlier?
You said he was a vampire, was he what you were after?"
"No, he certainly is part of my target, but putting The Dead back into the grave isn't my goal.
I only got him because he was a minion of my 'enemy'.
If I left him alone, he would kill more people to increase his power."

lines.japanese:
「……アルクェイド。
その、もっと俺にもわかるように説明してくれないか。
俺にはさっきの、あのおかしなヤツが人間なのかどうかもわからないんだ」
「そっか。
志貴にはまともに吸血鬼について話した事がなかったものね。
ネロは吸血鬼の中でも特異すぎた吸血種だから、説明する必要がなかったんだけど」
「……？
　まともな吸血鬼って、なにさ」
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
“Arcueid… could you explain this in a way I can understand? I don’t even know whether that bizarre thing was human.”
“I suppose I’ve never properly explained vampires to you. Nrvnqsr was such an anomalous vampiric species that the ordinary explanation hardly applied to him.” “Ordinary vampires? What does that mean?”
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… Arcueid.
Um, could you explain it so I can understand?
I don't even know if that guy was even human or not."
"Oh.
I guess I never really did explain to you in detail about vampires.
Nrvnqsr was sort of an aberration amongst the vampire race, so I didn't really need to explain it at that time."
"……?
What is a normal vampire then?"

lines.japanese:
「だから、あなた達が想像しているような吸血鬼のことよ。
不老不死で、人間の血を吸って、吸った者も吸血鬼にして使役し、太陽の光の前に敗退するっていうごく当たり前の吸血鬼。
　わたしの『敵』はね、そういう旧いタイプの吸血鬼なの」
「……えっと、つまりその『敵』っていうのが街で通り魔殺人をおこしてるヤツの事だよな」
「……どうかしらね。
実際に人を殺して血を吸っているのは、さっき始末したような『死者』の仕事かもしれない。
　志貴、ネロが体内に山ほどの使い魔を装備していたのは覚えてるでしょ？」
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
“The sort of vampire humans imagine. Ageless and immortal, drinking human blood, turning their victims into vampires and commanding them, then falling helpless before the sun—the perfectly conventional kind. My enemy is one of those old-fashioned vampires.” “So this ‘enemy’ is the one behind the killings in town, right?”
“Who knows? The actual killing and blood-drinking may be done by members of the Dead like the one I just destroyed. You remember how Nrvnqsr carried hordes of familiars inside his body, don’t you?”

lines.mirrorMoon:
"What I mean is what you all think of vampires.
Immortal, never aging, sucking human blood, turning that human into a vampire, being destroyed by sunlight, all of that.
My 'enemy' is that old type of vampire."
"…… Um, so you mean this 'enemy' of yours is the one behind all the recent serial killings?"
"…… I suppose.
But the killing of all those people by sucking their blood might be the work of "The Dead" like the one you saw earlier.
Shiki, you remember how Nrvnqsr's body was made of all those familiars, right?"

lines.japanese:
「―――ああ。
そう簡単に忘れられることじゃないよ、あれは」
「さっきの死者はそれと同じよ。
いい？
　吸血鬼に血を吸われ、その時に吸血鬼に血を送られると、その人間は死んでいるにもかかわらず現世に残ってしまうの。
これを死者といって、吸血鬼の一般的な使い魔とされるわ。
　あ、志貴にはゾンビっていったほうがわかりやすいかな。
アレは死体に寄生するハイチの白蛇のことだけど、動く死体っていったらゾンビが有名なんでしょ？」
―――うん、そう言われたほうがしゃっきりとイメージできる。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
“Of course. That isn’t something I’m likely to forget.”
“The Dead you saw works on the same principle. When a vampire drinks a human’s blood and then feeds that person some of its own, the victim remains in this world despite being dead. We call such a creature one of the Dead, and it serves as a vampire’s most common familiar. Perhaps ‘zombie’ would be easier for you. Strictly speaking, that refers to the Haitian white serpent that inhabits corpses, but zombies are your culture’s famous walking dead, aren’t they?”
Yes. Put that way, the image snaps instantly into focus.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"---Yeah, that's not exactly something I can easily forget."
"The Dead are like that.
When humans have their blood sucked by a vampire, they can also receive some of the vampire's blood.
They die, but remain in this world as a servant of the vampire.
They are called The Dead and they are like the vampire's familiars.
Ah, maybe it's easier to understand if I use the word zombie.
It's closer to the voodoo belief in Haiti where the white serpent-god Damballah is invoked to control a dead body, but let's just say a dead body that moves is a zombie, okay?"
---Yeah, I can visualize it better that way.

lines.japanese:
「わかった、つまりさっきの男はとっくの昔に吸血鬼に殺されてて、そのあとでゾンビにされてこき使われてるっていうコトなんだな？」
　そうそう、と満足そうに頷くアルクェイド。
「―――わかんないな。
吸血鬼ってのはどうしてそんなコトするんだよ。
殺した人間を―――殺しちまった人間をさ、そのまま生きかえらせてアゴで使うなんて、趣味が悪すぎる」
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
“I understand. So that man was killed by a vampire long ago, turned into a zombie, and worked like a slave ever since?”
Arcueid nods, delighted that I finally understand. “Why would vampires do something like that? Killing a person, dragging the corpse back to its feet, and ordering it around is grotesque.”

"I get it, so that man was killed by a vampire, who uses him as a zombie?"
"Yes, yes," Arcueid nods happily.
"---I'm still confused though.
Why would a vampire do that?
Killing people---not letting them die but controlling them, what bad taste."

lines.japanese:
「そうね。
吸血鬼が悪趣味なのは認めるわ。
でもそれは死徒に限った話よ。
初めから吸血種だったものはあまりそういうコトはしないもの」
「――――？」
　初めから、吸血鬼だったもの……？
「―――思い出した。
そういえば言ってたな、吸血鬼には二種類あるって。
初めから吸血鬼だったのと、人間から吸血鬼になった吸血鬼。
　……前に聞いた時、その話がひっかかってたんだ。
なんかおかしいなって。
そもそもさ、初めから吸血鬼じゃないって、それはどういうコトなんだ？」

lines.maoEnglish:
“I’ll concede that vampires have appalling taste. But that particular habit belongs to Dead Apostles. Those who were vampiric from birth rarely do such things.”
“What…?” Vampiric from birth?
“Now I remember. You said there were two kinds: those born as vampires, and those who began as humans. That bothered me the first time I heard it. What does it mean for a vampire not to have been one from the beginning?”

"You're right, those vampires do have bad taste.
But that's something only the Dead Apostles do.
Those that were always vampires from the very beginning do not do such things."
"----?"
Always vampires from the very beginning ……?
"---I remember.
You said there's two types of vampires, those who were vampires originally, and those who were humans.
…… When I heard that before, it kind of stuck in my head, I thought it was a little odd.
So what exactly do you mean by those who weren't originally vampires?"

lines.japanese:
「どういうコトもなにも、死徒はもともと人間だった者達よ。
魔術の果てに不老になったものと、真祖に血を吸われて下僕となったものとがいるわ。
　……志貴、貴方はさっき殺した人間を使役するのが悪趣味だと言ったけど、それでもまだマシなほうなのよ。
中にはもっと理解不能な遊びを考案する吸血鬼もいるんだから」
「―――遊びって―――なんだよ、それ。
おまえたちは遊びで人間を殺して、その死体を玩具にしてるっていうのか……！」
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: “Dead Apostles were human originally. Some attained agelessness at the furthest reaches of magecraft; others became thralls after a True Ancestor drank their blood. You called it grotesque to command the people you kill, Shiki, but that is one of their milder diversions. Some vampires invent games far less comprehensible.” “Games…? Are you saying you kill humans for amusement and make toys of their corpses?”

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Simple, I'm just saying that Dead Apostles used to be humans.
They either gained immortality through magic or became servants of the True Ancestors that sucked their blood.
…… Shiki, you said it was bad taste to use killed humans, but that's just the least of it.
There are other vampires who think up worse games."
"---A game---what is that?
You guys kill for fun, and use their dead bodies as toys……!?"

lines.japanese:
「……否定はしないわ。
　吸血鬼にとって『娯楽』は呼吸と同じことなのよ。
人間という連環種でありながら、不完全ながらも不老不死に近付いた彼らにとって最大の敵は“退屈”だったの。
　もともとわたし達と違って目的がないくせに“不老不死”になった彼らは、不老不死を手にいれた瞬間にあらゆる物欲がなくなってしまったのよ。
　目的が不老不死だったんだから、まあ仕方がないっていえば仕方がないんだろうけど」
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: “I won’t deny it. To a vampire, amusement is as necessary as breathing. Though born into the human species and its cycle, they drew close to ageless immortality—imperfectly—and discovered that their greatest enemy was boredom. Unlike us, they had no purpose beyond attaining immortality. The instant they achieved it, every material desire vanished. Immortality had been their only goal, so perhaps that result was inevitable.”

Immortality had been their only goal, so perhaps that result was inevitable.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… I won't deny that.
For vampires, "amusement" is the same as breathing.
For those who were once human but gain imperfect immortality, their greatest enemy is boredom.
They didn't have a reason to become immortal to start with, so once they gained immortality, they lost all kinds of greed.
Their goal was immortality itself, so I guess that's just the way things are."

lines.maoEnglish: “Don’t give me that nonsense about playing because they’re bored. If they never age and never die, isn’t that enough? Why would they need any other pleasure?” “Because it became enough. And that left their existence without meaning. Once a living thing recognizes itself as valueless—as something that has stopped—there is no longer any reason for it to exist. Ageless immortality is only another name for death.”

lines.japanese:
「だから彼らは段々と磨耗していって、自分たちから娯楽を作る事にした。
生きているんだって、自分たちはまだ楽しみがあるんだって自らを弁護するように。
―――それが、貴族の発端。
「彼らは人間の真似ごとをして、自分を城主にみたてて自らの勢力を広げるゲームを始めたわ。
　ありていに言ってしまえば死者の王国ね。
思いの外、それは彼らにとって刺激的だったみたい」
　……他人ごとのようにアルクェイドは言う。
　そういうアルクェイドだってその一人のはずなのに、どうも彼女にはそういった趣味はないみたいだ。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
“So they slowly wore away and began manufacturing amusements for themselves, as if to insist that they were still alive, that there were still pleasures open to them. That was the beginning of their aristocracy.”
“Imitating human society, they cast themselves as lords of castles and began a game of expanding their domains. Put simply, they built kingdoms of the Dead. It proved more stimulating than they expected.”
Arcueid speaks as if none of this concerns her. She ought to be one of them herself, yet she seems to have no taste for such games.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"So they started to wear down and they started to create their own amusement, as if to tell themselves they could have fun as long as they lived.

"They copy humans and see themselves in a game as lords of a castle expanding their territory.

It seems they got more enjoyment out of that than they expected."
…… She speaks as if she was talking of other people.
Arcueid should be one of those, but she certainly doesn't seem like she has that sort of hobby.

たえず他者から命を吸い上げないと不老不死ではいられない。
　不完全な不老不死だと言ったでしょ？
　死徒は結局、人間という捕食対象がいないと“不老不死”ではいられない」
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: “Now, this takes us backward, but Dead Apostles began as humans. A rare few became vampires after mastering magecraft, but most are victims whose blood was drunk. They are indeed ageless and immortal, but they are not perpetual motion machines. They must continually drain life from others to preserve that immortality. I told you it was imperfect. Without humans to prey upon, a Dead Apostle cannot remain immortal.”

They are indeed ageless and immortal, but they are not perpetual motion machines. They must continually drain life from others to preserve that immortality. I told you it was imperfect. Without humans to prey upon, a Dead Apostle cannot remain immortal.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Well, we'll change the topic, but the Dead Apostles were originally human.
There are a few cases where they became vampires through their own magical research, but the majority of them were humans who had their blood sucked.
They are immortal, but they can't last forever.
They can only be immortal if they drink the blood of others.
Didn't I say their immortality was imperfect?
If they can't feed on humans then their immortality is gone."

「けど、無闇に人間を捕食していると“吸血鬼”という自分の存在が明るみになってしまう。
そうでなくても死徒は活動しているだけで場を歪ませてしまうから、いずれシエルのような教会の代行者を呼び寄せてしまう」
「……えっと、それはつまり、吸血鬼は自分の好きなように活動できないっていうコト？」
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: “But feeding indiscriminately exposes the vampire’s existence. Even without that, a Dead Apostle distorts its surroundings merely by acting, and sooner or later that draws an executor of the Church—someone like Ciel.” “So vampires can’t simply do whatever they please?”

lines.mirrorMoon:
"But, if they openly fed on humans, then the existence of "vampires" would be revealed.
Even if they don't, just by being there, they distort the world around them.
That would attract the attention of agents of The Church, like Ciel."
"…… Um, so you mean that vampires can't do what they want?"

lines.japanese:
「そうね。
教会との契約を破って好き勝手に活動すれば、即座に発見されて消滅させられてしまう。
　だから死徒の大部分は、自分が眠ったままでも自分に人間の血肉を注ぎ込んでくれる分身を作り出す。
　血を吸って、自分の血を死体に送りこんで、自分の操り下僕として活動させる生者の擬態。
これをわたしたちは単純に“死者”って呼ぶのよ」
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: “Yes. If they break their pact with the Church and act as they please, they’re discovered and destroyed at once. Most Dead Apostles therefore create extensions of themselves—creatures that can continue supplying them with human blood and flesh while they sleep. They drain a victim, inject their own blood into the corpse, then set that counterfeit of the living to work as an obedient thrall. We simply call those creatures the Dead.”

Most Dead Apostles therefore create extensions of themselves—creatures that can continue supplying them with human blood and flesh while they sleep. They drain a victim, inject their own blood into the corpse, then set that counterfeit of the living to work as an obedient thrall. We simply call those creatures the Dead.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Yes, if they break their agreement with The Church and move about freely, they would be immediately discovered and annihilated.
So the majority of the Dead Apostles make subordinates that can bring them blood as they sleep.
Sucking blood and giving the dead body some blood of their own, they create their minions who do their work for them.
We simply call those "The Dead."

lines.japanese:
「……ふうん……それじゃあさっきアルクェイドが、その、始末した死者っていうのは死徒っていうヤツの兵士みたいなものなんだ」
「兵士っていうよりは人形ね。
本来なら血を吸われた人間が自力で吸血種として蘇生する過程を無視して、完全に死徒の分身として操っているんだから。
　死者は親である死徒と繋がっているわ。
　死者だって自らが生存するためのエネルギーを必要とするから人間を襲い、肉をすする。
けど、その半分以上は親元である死徒に流れていくのよ。
　ようするに女王蜂を養う働き蜂みたいなものね。
死者を操る死徒は、自分の棺の中で眠っているだけで力を蓄えてしまえるのよ」
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
“I see… So the Dead you disposed of was something like a soldier serving a Dead Apostle.”
“More like a puppet. Ordinarily, a person drained of blood must pass through the process of reviving as a vampiric being under their own power. The Dead bypass that process and are controlled entirely as extensions of their parent Dead Apostle. Each remains connected to its parent. It attacks humans and devours flesh for the energy it needs to survive, but more than half of what it takes flows back to the Dead Apostle. Think of worker bees feeding a queen. The master can gather strength without doing anything but sleeping in its coffin.”

The master can gather strength without doing anything but sleeping in its coffin.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hmm…… So what you killed before was kind of like a soldier for the Dead Apostles?"
"Not so much a soldier as a puppet.
The Dead Apostles control the dead bodies by skipping the process of becoming a vampire.
The Dead are completely connected to their parent vampire.
In order for them to survive, they attack others to eat their flesh, but more than half of that energy goes to their master.
Like a queen bee nourished by the worker bees, the Dead Apostles can use The Dead to increase their power while they sleep."

lines.japanese:
「……わたしの『敵』が簡単には見つからないのは、『敵』が死者を多く使っているから。
　あいつが自分の手を汚すのは一回だけ。
あとは死者にした人間を操って、自分は眠っているだけで領地を広げていく。
―――通り魔殺人による遺体が何体も発見されてるって言うけど、あんなのは偽造に失敗しただけのものよ。
　実際、この街の犠牲者は百人を超えているわ。
ひっそりと、人知れずいなくなってしまっている人達の一部分が、あなたたちが騒いでいる犠牲者っていうことね」
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: “My enemy is difficult to find because it employs so many of the Dead. It soils its own hands only once. After that, it controls the human it has turned and expands its territory while it sleeps. You’ve heard that several bodies from the serial killings have been discovered, but those are merely the victims it failed to turn into the Dead. In truth, this town has suffered more than a hundred victims. The handful of bodies causing such a commotion are only a fraction of all the people who have vanished quietly, without anyone knowing why.”

In truth, this town has suffered more than a hundred victims. lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… My 'enemy' can't be found easily because he's using a lot of The Dead.
He only dirties his hands once.
After that, he simply controls The Dead while he sleeps and expands his territory.
---They say many bodies are found in the recent supposed serial killings, but those are actually just failures.
To tell the truth, there are over a hundred victims in this city.
But only a small amount, the ones discovered, are the victims in the news."

More than a hundred? That many people have been drained and killed by a vampire? And those victims become blood-drinking monsters themselves, strolling casually through town like that man did?

「………ふざけ、てる」
　三日前。
　ホテルに泊まっていた人々が、それこそ何の意味もなく殺され尽くしたのを、思い出す。
　俺はあのホテルにいたけれど、その場面を見ていない。
だから言葉の上でしか想像できず、ソレがどんなに憎むべき暴力であったかを肌で感じ取れなかった。
　今だってそれは同じだ。
　人間の血を吸う吸血鬼がいて、そいつが少しずつ自分の領地を広げているなんて聞いても、実感はわかない。

lines.maoEnglish: “That’s… sick.” I remember the hotel three days ago, where every guest had been slaughtered for no reason at all. I was there, but I never saw the massacre itself. I could imagine it only through words, never feel upon my skin the vileness of that violence. Even now, it is the same. Hearing that a vampire drinks human blood and is slowly expanding its territory through the city doesn’t feel real.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"……… That's ridiculous."
Three days ago.
I remember how all those people in the hotel were killed for no reason.
I was there but I didn't see it, so I can only visualize and can't really tell what kind of violence it was.
It's still the same.
I can't fathom the existence of vampires that suck human blood, just to increase their own territory.

―――ただ。
　何の理由も、どんな前触れもなく、例えば自分のもっとも身近な人間がそんなふうに殺されたら、俺はどうなってしまうだろうか。
　想像したくもないのに、ほんのわずかだけ。
　血を吸われて、それこそゴミのようにうち捨てられている秋葉の姿を想像する。
「くっ――――」
　あたまにくるのは―――そんな最悪な出来事がもう今にだって起きえるのだというこの街の状況と、それに気がつきもしなかった自分自身の平和さだ。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
But suppose someone closest to me were murdered that way, without reason or warning. What would become of me? Though I don’t want to imagine it, the image flashes through my mind: Akiha drained of blood and discarded like garbage.
“Ghh…” What enrages me is that such a nightmare could happen at any moment in this town—and that I had lived in peace without ever noticing.

without reason, without even recognition, if someone close to me died like that, how would I act?

I imagine Akiha being drained of blood and discarded like trash.
"K----"
What makes me mad---is that this worst case scenario could happen at any minute in this town and I didn't even have a clue about it before.

「やっぱり怒ったわね、志貴。
　……わたしがあんまり話したくなかったのは、これは捕食される側――あなたたちにとっては一切の言い訳も許さない『悪』そのものだからよ。
　志貴にとっては気持ちのいい話じゃなかったでしょう？」
「――――まあ、な。
そんな話を聞いたら、これからどうしていいのかわからなくなる」
　……そう。
　明日にでも親しい人が犠牲者になるかもしれない街で、今までどおり平和に暮らしていけるハズがない。
　知ってしまったのなら。
　俺は、ネロの時みたいに戦わなくちゃいけない。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: “I knew you would be angry, Shiki. I didn’t want to tell you because, to the prey—to humans—this is evil itself, beyond any possible excuse. It wasn’t pleasant to hear, was it?” “Yeah. Hearing all this makes it impossible to know what I should do next.” That’s right. I can’t go on living peacefully as before in a town where someone dear to me may become tomorrow’s victim. Now that I know, I have to fight, just as I did against Nrvnqsr.

lines.japanese:
「だから、あとは当初の予定どおりこの街に潜んでいる『敵』を見つけて、なんとか始末してみせるわ。
　志貴は今までどおり普通の生活に戻って、わたしたちなんかに関わらなくていいんだよ」
　何が嬉しいのか、アルクェイドはまっすぐな笑顔を向けて、そんな事を言った。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: “So all that remains is to follow my original plan: find the enemy hiding in this town and destroy it somehow. You can return to your ordinary life, Shiki. You don’t need to involve yourself with creatures like us anymore.” For some reason, she says it with a perfectly open smile.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"So now I can go back to the original plan and defeat my 'enemy'.
You can go back to living your normal life now, and you don't have to associate with me anymore."
She smiles as if she is happy about something.

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: Arcueid tells Shiki to return to ordinary life and stop involving himself with 'the likes of us'—the vampire world. mirror moon changes the plural category into Arcueid alone, turning a safety warning into a much more personal rejection at the moment their alliance is being renegotiated.
mirrorMoonErrors.title: Leaving vampires behind becomes leaving Arcueid personally

lines.japanese:
「……………」
「志貴？
　なによ、また難しい顔しちゃって」
「そりゃあ難しい顔ぐらいする。
だって、これは俺たちの住んでる街の問題なんだから」
「だから気にしなくていいんだって。
二三日じゅうになんとかするから、もうこれ以上は犠牲者は出させないわ」
　ああ、正直こっちだって関わり合いになんかなりたくない。
―――でも、その台詞は。
　この街を守るようなその台詞は、アルクェイドではなくこの街に住んでいる俺が、言わなくちゃいけないコトじゃないんだろうか。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
“…”
“Shiki? Why the serious face again?” “Because this is serious. It’s happening in the town where we live.”
“That’s why I said you don’t need to worry. I’ll settle it within two or three days. I won’t allow any more victims.”
Honestly, I want nothing to do with this. But those words—words about protecting this town—shouldn’t they be spoken by someone who lives here, rather than by Arcueid? Shouldn’t they be mine?

"……………"
"Shiki?

lines.japanese:
「……アルクェイド。
その、一つ聞くけど。
おまえの言ってる『敵』っていうのは強いのか？」
「さっきの死者よりは格段に優れているでしょうね。
今回はまだ出会っていないからわからないけど、八年間も潜んでいたんだから第五階級ぐらいにはなってるんじゃないかな」
「……第五階級って、よくわからないけど。
もしかしてネロより強いのか、そいつ」
「まさか。
ネロは別格よ。
あいつは私がまともな時でも倒しきれない最高純度の吸血種よ。
それに比べれば、わたしの敵はいくぶん格が落ちるわ」
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: “Arcueid, let me ask one thing. Is this enemy of yours strong?” “Far stronger than the Dead you saw. I haven’t encountered it yet this time, so I can’t be certain, but after hiding for eight years, it has probably reached the fifth rank.” “I don’t know what the fifth rank means. Is it stronger than Nrvnqsr?” “Of course not. Nrvnqsr was exceptional—a vampiric being of the highest purity whom I could not reliably defeat even at full strength. My enemy is several grades beneath him.”

lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… Arcueid.
Um, can I ask a question?
This 'enemy' you speak of, is he strong?"
"Well, he should be many times superior to The Dead earlier.
I haven't met him this time, but he has been latent for eight years so maybe he's a Class Five by now."
"…… Class Five?
I don't get it, but does that mean he's stronger than Nrvnqsr?"
"Not a chance.
Nrvnqsr was special.
He was a pure, supreme vampire that would be difficult to defeat even with my full power.
Compared to him, this enemy is pretty weak."

lines.japanese:
「――――そうか。
それなら―――おまえがやられるっていう事、ないよな」
　安堵のためか、はあ、と大きく息をはいた。
「さあ、どうでしょうね。
ちょっと前までのわたしなら問題なかったと思うけど、今のわたしは病み上がりだもの。
アイツのほうが力をつけている可能性は高いわ」
「……病み上がりって、風邪でもひいたのかアルクェイド」
「うん、どうにも志貴に殺された後遺症がぬけきらなくて。
このぶんじゃあと何日かはダメみたい」
「――――あ」
　そうか――アルクェイドが弱っているのは、他の誰でもなく、この俺の責任だった。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
“I see. Then… there’s no chance it could kill you.” Relief escapes me in a long breath.
“Who knows? A short while ago, I would have had no trouble. But I’m still recovering, and there’s a good chance my enemy has grown stronger.” “Recovering? Did you catch a cold or something?” “Yeah. I just can’t seem to shake off the effects of being killed by you. At this rate, I’ll be in poor condition for several more days.” “Ah…” Of course. Arcueid’s weakness is no one’s fault but mine.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"----Oh.
Then---there's no way you'll be defeated."
I breathe out in relief.
"Hm, who knows?
A few days earlier and he wouldn't be a problem, but now I'm just recovering.
The possibility that he has more power is actually high."
"…… Recovering?
Are you sick or something, Arcueid?"
"Yeah, I still have the effects from when you killed me and I don't think I'll be fine for at least a few more days."
"----Ah."
That's right--the reason why Arcueid is weak… it isn't anyone's fault but mine.

lines.maoEnglish:
“About what we were discussing earlier, Arcueid.” “What part?” “Whether I was taking your side or hers.”
“Wait. Hear me out before you react. You are completely divorced from common sense, hopelessly selfish, and almost impossible to manage.”
Arcueid narrows her eyes, looking more displeased by the second. I press on anyway, surrendering to momentum and saying exactly what I feel.

lines.maoEnglish:
“So what do we do now? Walk the streets again and look for more of the Dead?”
“For now, that’s about all we can do. The man just now made twelve, so there can’t be many of the Dead left. Once we destroy every one in the city, the vampire who spawned them will have no choice but to come out. Until then, we keep hunting the survivors.” Arcueid’s eyes ask whether I’m all right with that.
lines.mao_english:

Once we destroy every one in the city, the vampire who spawned them will have no choice but to come out. Until then, we keep hunting the survivors.” Arcueid’s eyes ask whether I’m all right with that.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"But, what do we do now?
Do you want to search for more of The Dead like before?"
"Yeah, I think that's all we can do for now.
The one before was the twelfth, so I don't think there's many more.
The parent vampire will have to come out once they all are destroyed, so we have to hunt the remaining ones for now.
Is that still okay?", she asks.

lines.japanese:
「いいもなにも、俺はアルクェイドに付き合うだけだよ。
アルクェイドがそうするっていうんなら、大人しくしたがうさ。
――じゃ、もう一度街に行くか」
「あ、今夜はもういいの。
効率よく死者を操るためにはね、それなりの活動ルートを定めているもので、一晩に複数の死者は活動させないと思う。
　ただでさえ数が減ってきているんだから、むこうも無闇に活動させないでしょうし」
「―――そうなの？
　でも、それじゃあアルクェイドから死者を隠そうとするんじゃないのか、その『敵』ってヤツは」
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: “It isn’t for me to object. I’m following your lead, Arcueid. If that’s what you want, I’ll behave and do as I’m told. So—shall we head back into town?” “Oh, we’re done for tonight. To control the Dead efficiently, you establish routes for them, and I doubt our enemy would send more than one out in a single night. Their numbers are already dwindling, so there’s even less reason to waste them.” “Really? But then wouldn’t this ‘enemy’ just hide the rest from you?”

So—shall we head back into town?” “Oh, we’re done for tonight. To control the Dead efficiently, you establish routes for them, and I doubt our enemy would send more than one out in a single night. Their numbers are already dwindling, so there’s even less reason to waste them.” “Really? But then wouldn’t this ‘enemy’ just hide the rest from you?”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Anything is fine, I'm just with you.
If you lead, then I'll follow.
--Well, shall we start again?"
"Ah, no, that's good for tonight.
They usually follow a fixed route, and the other Dead will probably not be out tonight.
Since they are fewer in number, I don't think he'll let them all come out at once."
"---Oh really?
But, doesn't that mean this 'enemy' will try to hide The Dead from you, Arcueid?"

「基本的にはね。
けど、『敵』が吸血鬼である以上、どうしても他者から血や精を搾取しないと存在してられないのよ。
　だから、むこうはわたしに狙われてるってわかっていても、最低限の食料を得るために死者を出すしかないっていうわけ」
―――はあ。
　で、その最低限の死者が、さっきの男性だったわけか。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
“That would be the sensible thing. But a vampire can’t survive without draining blood and vital essence from others. Even knowing I’m hunting it, our enemy still has to send out the Dead to secure the bare minimum of food.”
—I see. So the man back there had been that bare minimum.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Basically.
But since this 'enemy' is a vampire, he needs to steal the blood and energy of others.
So, even though he knows I'm searching for them, he has to send The Dead out to get the minimal blood he needs."
---*sigh*
Then, the minimal Dead he sent out was that man from before, huh.

「そういうこと。
だから今夜は、これ以上探し回っても無駄だと思う」
「……まあ、俺はどうでもいいけど。
なんだかまだるっこしいな、それ」
「ええ。
もともと吸血鬼退治は面倒なものなの。
この街のどこかにある『敵』の棺を探しあてるんだから、そう簡単には終わらないわ」
　アルクェイドは俺から手を離すと、タン、という軽い足取りでうしろに跳んだ。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
“Exactly. Which means there’s no point searching any longer tonight.” “Fine by me, but this is awfully slow going.” “Hunting vampires always is. We have to find our enemy’s coffin somewhere in this entire city. It was never going to end quickly.”
Arcueid releases my hand and springs lightly backward.
lines.mao_english:
“Exactly. Which means there’s no point searching any longer tonight.” “Fine by me, but this is awfully slow going.” “Hunting vampires always is. We have to find our enemy’s coffin somewhere in this entire city. It was never going to end quickly.”
Arcueid releases my hand and springs lightly backward.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"So, searching further tonight will be useless, I think."
"…… Well, I don't mind.
It is tedious though."
"Yeah, hunting vampires is tedious work.
We have to find the coffin of this 'enemy' somewhere in this city, so it won't be easy."
Arcueid lets go of my hand and jumps back softly.

lines.japanese:
「アルクェイド……？」
「今夜はここでお別れにしましょう。
どうせ、またすぐ明日に会えるんだから」
　アルクェイドは踊るようなステップで、こっちを見たまま遠ざかっていく。
「明日って―――ちょっと待て、待ち合わせ場所とかどうするんだよ……！」
「ここでいいよ。
時間は―――そうね、十時ごろがちょうどいいかな」
　笑顔で、実にかってに約束をする。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
“Arcueid…?”
“Let’s say good night here. We’ll be seeing each other again tomorrow anyway.” She dances away in buoyant little steps, still facing me. “Tomorrow—wait! Where are we even supposed to meet?”
“Right here is fine. As for the time… I think ten should be perfect.” Beaming, she makes the arrangement entirely on her own.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Arcueid……?"
"Let's say goodbye for tonight.
We'll meet tomorrow.
With her dance-like steps, she watches me as she gets farther away.
"Tomorrow---wait, where should we meet……!?"
"Here's fine.
The time---yeah, around ten o'clock should be fine."
With a smile, she makes that promise.

また明日、ここでね！
　と。

lines.maoEnglish: “Good night, Shiki. See you right here tomorrow!” With that, Arcueid waves and leaves.

lines.japanese:
―――屋敷に帰ってきた。
　時刻は夜の一時半。
　屋敷の明かりは、完全に消え去っている。
「………まずい、かな」
　屋敷の門に手をかける。
　がちん、という音。
　門には頑丈そうな錠が内側からかけられていた。
「―――まいったな。
切るわけにもいかないし」
　少し悩む。
　悩んでから、門を自力でよじのぼる事にした。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
—I made it back to the mansion. It was half past one in the morning, and every light in the house had gone out.
“…This could be bad.” I tried the front gate. Clank. A formidable-looking lock had been fastened on the inside.
“Wonderful. It’s not as if I can cut through it.” After a moment’s thought, I resigned myself to climbing the gate.
lines.mao_english:
—I made it back to the mansion. It was half past one in the morning, and every light in the house had gone out.
“…This could be bad.” I tried the front gate. Clank. A formidable-looking lock had been fastened on the inside.
“Wonderful. It’s not as if I can cut through it.” After a moment’s thought, I resigned myself to climbing the gate.
lines.mirrorMoon:
---I get back to the mansion.
It's about one-thirty in the morning.
The mansion is completely dark.
"……… This can't be good."
I put my hand on the mansion gate.
Ka-chang.
A sturdy chain holds it closed.
"---Dang.
I shouldn't cut this."
I think a bit.
Then, I decide to climb over the gate.

……疲れた。
　ドロボウさんよろしくで門をよじ登って、玄関にたどり着く。
　門は鍵がかかっていたが、玄関の扉は開いていた。
「……翡翠、ちゃんと開けててくれたんだ」
　ほう、と感謝の吐息がもれる。
　秋葉や琥珀さんたちを起こさないように、抜き足で屋敷の中へと入っていった。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
…That was exhausting. After scaling the gate like a common burglar, I reached the front entrance. The gate had been locked, but the front door was open. “…Hisui left it open for me.” A grateful sigh escaped me.
I crept inside on tiptoe, careful not to wake Akiha, Kohaku, or anyone else.

lines.mirrorMoon:
…… I'm exhausted.
After sneaking over the wall like a thief, I quietly make my way to the doorway.
The gate was locked, but the door isn't.
"…… It must have been Hisui."
I give a sigh of thanks.
So as not to wake Akiha, Kohaku-san or Hisui, I sneak my way through the mansion.

　一息ついて、ベッドに腰をかける。
「………………」
　アルクェイドとの約束。
　なんの因果か、また厄介なコトに足を踏み入れた遠野志貴。
「――――仕方ないじゃないか。
だってさ、放っておけなかったんだから」
　それとも、放っておきたくなかったのか。
「そりゃあ……アルクェイドのことは、好きだけど」
　けど、それって愛情なんだろうか。
　自分の気持ちがよく解らない。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
“Whew…” I sat on the edge of the bed and caught my breath. “……” My promise to Arcueid. By some perversity of fate, Shiki Tohno had gone and entangled himself in trouble all over again.
“What else could I do? I couldn’t just leave her to it.” Or had I simply not wanted to? “I mean… I do like Arcueid.” But was that love? I couldn’t make sense of my own feelings.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"------Whew."
Letting out a breath, I lay down on my bed.
"………………"
My promise to Arcueid.
Maybe it's fate, but you've gotten yourself tangled up in trouble again, Tohno Shiki.
"----Could I help it?
I just can't leave her alone."
Or maybe I didn't want to leave her alone?
"Well…… I do like Arcueid."
But is that love?
I don't even know my feelings.

ともかく、明日からまたアルクェイドの手伝いをする事になったんだ。
　今は余計なことは考えず、ゆっくりと体を休めて明日にそなえるとしよう――――
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: Whatever the answer, I was going to be helping Arcueid again starting tomorrow. For now, I would put every useless thought aside, rest properly, and save my strength for tomorrow—
lines.mao_english: Whatever the answer, I was going to be helping Arcueid again starting tomorrow. For now, I would put every useless thought aside, rest properly, and save my strength for tomorrow—
lines.mirrorMoon:
At any rate, it looks like I'll be helping Arcueid once again starting tomorrow.
So for now, I shouldn't think of anything else but getting a good night's sleep----
lines.mirror_moon:

―――眠れない。
　目を閉じると、なにか色々なものが浮かんでくる。
　アルクェイドのこと。
　この街に巣くっている吸血鬼のこと。
　……黒い法衣姿の、先輩のこと。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: —I couldn’t sleep. Whenever I closed my eyes, one thing after another floated into view. Arcueid. The vampire nesting somewhere in the city. And the girl from school, clad in black vestments…
lines.mao_english: —I couldn’t sleep. Whenever I closed my eyes, one thing after another floated into view. Arcueid. The vampire nesting somewhere in the city. And the girl from school, clad in black vestments…
lines.mirrorMoon:
---I can't sleep.
If I close my eyes, so many things come to mind.
About Arcueid.
About this vampire lurking the streets.
…… About the black-clothed Senpai.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.maoEnglish: “……” No. I couldn’t sleep. At times like this, there was nothing for it but a book. I was sure I had left one half-finished the other day—

lines.japanese: 一番初めの感情は、むしろ憐憫だった。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: The first emotion I felt was, more than anything, pity.
lines.mao_english: The first emotion I felt was, more than anything, pity.
lines.mirrorMoon: The first feeling was rather one of pity.
lines.mirror_moon: The first feeling was rather one of pity.

lines.japanese:
怒りでも失望でもない。
　ただ、目にうつるすべてのものが哀れに思えた。
（無論、最も哀れなのはこの身ではあるのだが）
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish: Not anger. Not disappointment. Everything my eyes beheld merely struck me as pitiful. Naturally, this body of mine was the most pitiful thing of all.
lines.mao_english: Not anger. Not disappointment. Everything my eyes beheld merely struck me as pitiful. Naturally, this body of mine was the most pitiful thing of all.
lines.mirrorMoon:
Not anger, not despair.
Just, I thought everything before my eyes was pitiful.
(Of course, the most pitiful thing is myself.)

lines.japanese:
際限なく壊れていく命。
　際限なく薄れていく営み。
　際限なく忘れていく時間。
　みな落ちるだけだ。
　なのに懸命に存在しようとあがき、それが叶わぬと識ると生み続ける。
　生み出し続ける。
　結局、それらさえ亡くなるというのに、それではあまりにも報われない。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
Lives breaking without end. Human endeavor fading without end. Time forgotten without end.
Everything only falls away. Yet all things struggle desperately to remain, and when they learn that cannot be, they beget more life. They go on creating. Those creations will perish in turn, of course. The whole endeavor is too cruelly unrewarded.
lines.mao_english:
Lives breaking without end. Human endeavor fading without end. Time forgotten without end.
Everything only falls away. Yet all things struggle desperately to remain, and when they learn that cannot be, they beget more life. They go on creating. Those creations will perish in turn, of course. The whole endeavor is too cruelly unrewarded.
lines.mirrorMoon:
Life which breaks down without limit.
Daily life which fades without limit.
Time which is forgotten without limit.
Everyone only falls.
And yet everyone still struggles desperately to continue existing, and when they judge that it is not possible, they continue to reproduce.
Continuing to reproduce.
In the end, even that dies, but there is no recompensation.

lines.japanese:
無論、死にゆく存在が報われないのではない。
　我々には初めから救いなどない。
　報われないのは、その試み。
　永遠を望もうとする、気高い、およそ一文にもならぬほど需要のない、誰も求めてなぞいない祈りだ。
　壊れていくものには一切の興味はない。
　もし私に死というものが視覚でき理解できるのならば、多少の関心はもてるだろうが。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
Not that the dying themselves go unrewarded. There was never any salvation for us to begin with. What goes unrewarded is the attempt: the noble prayer for eternity, worth less than a penny because no one has any use for it—a prayer no one ever asked to hear.
Things that break hold no interest for me. Perhaps they would inspire some small curiosity if I could see death and comprehend it.
lines.mao_english:
Not that the dying themselves go unrewarded. There was never any salvation for us to begin with. What goes unrewarded is the attempt: the noble prayer for eternity, worth less than a penny because no one has any use for it—a prayer no one ever asked to hear.
Things that break hold no interest for me. Perhaps they would inspire some small curiosity if I could see death and comprehend it.
lines.mirrorMoon:
Of course, it is not those who die who are not recompensated.
We had no hope to begin with.
What is not recompensated are the attempts.
The noble wish, the yearning for eternity which everyone longs for yet can not achieve.
I have no interest whatsoever in the things that break down.
If I could see death and understand it, maybe I'll take a bit of an interest.

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: The speaker calls the prayer for eternity noble but so lacking in demand that it is not worth a penny—something nobody is asking for. mirror moon says exactly the opposite, that everyone longs for it, reversing the premise of the surrounding meditation on an unrewarded and almost ridiculous prayer.
mirrorMoonErrors.title: A prayer nobody wants becomes the yearning everyone shares

およそ計測不可能なほど繰り返され、なお繰り返されるその祈り。
　もはや滑稽とさえされるその祈りを、ただ一つの清らかなものに代えようと思った。
　方法は言うまでもない。
　祈りは、叶えられた時点で結果となる。
　それだけを目的として生きてきた。
　別段信念があったわけではない。
　私が最初に覚えた言葉が、永遠という単語であっただけの話だ。
lines.label: s259
lines.maoEnglish:
That prayer, repeated beyond all measure and then repeated still, had long since become an object of ridicule. I resolved to transform it into the one pure thing in this world.
The means hardly need stating. The moment a prayer is granted, it ceases to be a prayer and becomes a result.
I lived for that purpose alone. Not from any particular conviction. It merely happened that the first word I ever learned was eternity.
